away.name: Brandon Bussi
away.news: Bussi had a surprising breakout last season as a 27-year-old rookie, ultimately leading the Hurricanes to a Stanley Cup Championship. However, early-season struggles and outstanding play from counterpart Pytor Kochetkov have made Bussi a secondary option in 2026-27. The 28-year-old Bussi has played only once in the past three weeks, but he was serviceable, saving 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%) in a 5-3 win over the New York Islanders. The Hurricanes enter Thursday's game as significant -286 road favourites against the Seattle Kraken, who are 2-3-0 in their past five games.

home.name: Philipp Grubauer
home.news: Grubauer had an encouraging start to the 2026-27 season, but has returned to the inconsistent play that has made him a secondary option in recent seasons. The 34-year-old German goalie has started only once in the past two weeks, in a game where he allowed four goals on 14 shots (.714 SV%) in a 6-2 loss to the Calgary Flames. The Kraken enter Thursday's game as sizeable +248 home favourites against the Eastern Conference-leading Carolina Hurricanes.

away.name: Jacob Fowler
away.news: Fowler was outstanding in the opening month of the season, posting a 1.84 GAA and .932 SV% in eight October games (7-1-0). That said, he had a catastrophic meltdown in his first game of November, as the Montreal Canadiens blew a 4-0 lead over the Winnipeg Jets in the final three minutes of an eventual 5-4 overtime loss. That said, the 21-year-old Fowler wasn't phased by the loss, bouncing back in his next two games (1-0-1), saving 48 of 52 shots (.923 SV%).

home.name: Jeremy Swayman
home.news: Jeremy Swayman had a miserable 2024-25 season after signing a massive eight-year contract extension, posting an ugly 3.11 GAA and .892 SV% in 58 games (22-29-7). That said, he followed it up with a solid 2025-26 season and has started 2026-27 as one of the top goalies in the NHL. The 27-year-old Swayman was outstanding in his most recent outing, saving 41 of 42 shots (.976 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Florida Panthers. He has allowed two or fewer goals in seven of 13 games this season. The Bruins enter Thursday's game as -119 home favourites against the Montreal Canadiens, who are coming off a 2-1 overtime loss to the Minnesota Wild.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has deservedly been the busiest goalie in the NHL this season, playing 17 of 20 games, posting a tremendous 1.93 GAA and .925 SV% with a 12-2-3 record. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie was excellent in Minnesota's previous game, saving 27 of 28 shots (.964 SV%) in a 2-1 overtime win against the Montreal Canadiens. He has allowed two or fewer goals in four straight games. The Wild enter Thursday's game as -169 road favourites against a struggling Toronto Maple Leafs team that is amid a four-game losing streak.

home.name: Anthony Stolarz
home.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has struggled, and Stolarz has been the more reliable option on most nights. The 32-year-old Stolarz has a solid 2.26 GAA and .929 SV% in his last four games (3-1-0). The Maple Leafs enter Thursday's game as +149 home underdogs against the Central Division-leading Minnesota Wild, who are riding a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Scott Wedgewood
away.news: Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, with a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), was expected to earn him at least a timeshare in 2026-27, but he has struggled immensely this season. The 34-year-old Wedgewood has not played since November 3, when he was pulled midway through the game after allowing four goals on nine shots (.556 SV%) in a 7-2 loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. He has allowed three or more goals in four of five games this season (1-3-1). The Avalanche enter Thursday's game as -101 road underdogs against the Ottawa Senators, who are 2-0-1 in their past three games.

home.name: Linus Ullmark
home.news: Ullmark has not played since suffering a lower-body injury on October 21st, with Samuel Ersson helping the Senators stay afloat during his absence. That said, the team is eager for Ullmark to return to the crease, given his outstanding start to the 2026-27 season. The 33-year-old Ullmark has a dazzling 1.33 GAA and .945 SV% in eight games (7-1-0). The Senators enter Thursday's game as slight -106 home favourites against a Colorado Avalanche team that has outscored opponents 10-3 in its past two games (2-0-0).

home.name: Akira Schmid
home.news: Schmid has been serviceable for Florida this season and kept his team afloat during a multi-week stint when Jacob Markstrom was sidelined with an injury. That said, the 26-year-old Schmid struggled in his most recent outing, allowing four goals on 31 shots (.871 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the Washington Capitals. Still, he has a solid 2.26 GAA and .911 SV% in his last four games (3-1-0). The Panthers enter Thursday's game as -164 home favourites against a Detroit Red Wings team that has scored just five total goals during a four-game losing streak.

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Skinner has been inconsistent this season, as he has been for most of his career, but he is on a three-game winning streak, posting a 2.96 GAA and an .870 SV%. That said, the 28-year-old goalie has allowed three or more goals in four of his past five games (2-3-0). The Jets enter Thursday's game as +153 road underdogs against a Dallas Stars team that beat them 3-2 in overtime earlier this season, a game in which Skinner saved 35 of 38 shots (.921 SV%).

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: The well-rested Stars return to action on Thursday against the Winnipeg Jets. The Stars last played on November 7th, when Oettinger saved 20 of 23 shots (.870 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the San Jose Sharks. The 27-year-old Oettinger leads the NHL with three shutouts, but he has battled some adversity lately, allowing three or more goals in four of his last five games (4-1-0). The Stars enter Thursday's game as -170 home favourites against a surging Winnipeg Jets team riding a four-game winning streak.

home.name: Karel Vejmelka
home.news: While rookie Sebastian Cossa has played well at times for the Mammoth, he has lacked consistency and has failed to earn more starts despite Karel Vejmelka's ongoing struggles. Vejmelka has allowed three or more goals in six straight games (1-5-0), posting an ugly .840 SV%. In his most recent outing, the 30-year-old Czech goalie allowed three goals on 20 shots (.850 SV%) in a 4-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators. The Mammoth enter Thursday's contest as slight -108 home favourites against the St. Louis Blues, who have lost three of their past four games (1-2-1).
